entities.summary:
Mary Anne Theisen-Lappen, born in 1989, emerged as a preeminent American weightlifter during the 2010s, significantly elevating the profile of women's strength sports both nationally and internationally. Her career, marked by numerous national titles and formidable international performances, positioned her as a trailblazer who consistently pushed the boundaries of American records in Olympic weightlifting. Theisen-Lappen's dedication and competitive spirit helped to reshape perceptions of female athleticism, inspiring a new generation of women to pursue strength sports at elite levels and challenging traditional gender norms within the broader athletic landscape.

Throughout her competitive career, Theisen-Lappen achieved remarkable success. A highlight was her silver medal performance at the 2015 Pan American Games in Toronto, Canada, competing in the 69 kg category, where she lifted a total of 220 kg (98 kg snatch, 122 kg clean & jerk). She was also a multiple-time USA Weightlifting National Champion, securing titles across different weight classes (e.g., 69 kg and 75 kg) and consistently setting new American records in the snatch, clean & jerk, and total. Her participation in several International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) World Championships further solidified her status as a global competitor, representing the United States against the world's best.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Mary Theisen-Lappen was a prominent figure in American weightlifting, setting national records and securing international medals which significantly boosted the sport's profile for women in the 2010s. Her achievements helped inspire greater participation and redefined perceptions of female strength within sports.
